hints: Fill cells from top to bottom and left to right.
For cell (r,c), inspect values already used earlier in row r and earlier in column c.
Choose the smallest nonnegative value absent from both sets.
analogy: At each square, choose the first number not already seen to its left or above.
algorithm: Scan row-major. Mark values present to the left in this row and above in this column, then select the smallest unmarked integer and print it.
correctness: The selection is by definition the least nonnegative value missing from both required directions, and scanning order ensures those cells are already assigned.
complexity: O(n^3) time with direct scanning and O(n^2) grid space; for n<=100 this is sufficient.
example: For a 2x2 grid, first row is 0,1; second row begins 1; the last cell is 0 because neither its left cell nor its upper cell contains 0.
